ROOT EXPLICIT COMPLETION OF THE SELECTOR (not a new height theorem):
Let F(theta)=log sum_Gamma exp(theta.x)/x!-m.theta. For suppliedB>=1 set tau=epsilon/(32B), G=F+tau||theta||2^2/2. Gradient monotonicity gives ||theta_tau||<3B, hence gradF(theta_tau)=-tau theta_tau; no covariance lower bound/interior promise needed. Obtain a rational M>=1 bounding HessianG on the slightly larger box[-4B-1,4B+1]^d by the paid Poisson-anchor moments; log M=poly_R(L+B). Start the cutting polytope atK0=[-4B,4B]^d. Put D=8dB+1, g0=epsilon/16,
 delta=min(g0/4,tau*g0^2/(16M^2D)), mu=tau*g0^2/(8M^2),
 r0=min(B/2,mu/[2(MD+1)]).
DDB1 moment calls plus rational exponential evaluation provide dyadic approximations gtilde to gradG of Euclidean error<=delta, fixed precision/magnitude bit lengths poly_R(L+B).

Maintain a rational bounded polytopeK. At each stage enumerate its vertices by d-facet intersections, choose a MAXIMUM-volume vertex simplex, and query at that simplex's rational centroidc. If ||gtilde||2<=g0, then ||gradF(c)||infinity<=epsilon/4. Otherwise add the CENTRAL cut gtilde.(theta-c)<=0. Strong convexity, ||c-theta_tau||<=D and smoothness give gtilde.(c-theta_tau)>=mu; therefore EVERY such cut retains the radius-r0 ball abouttheta_tau.

This rational cut is quantitatively deep without invoking a free ellipsoid oracle. If S is the maximum vertex simplex and c its centroid, every point ofK has absolute barycentric coordinates<=1 (otherwise replace a vertex to increase volume). Hence volK<=2^d*d!*volS. For T=c+(S-c)/d, both T and its reflection aboutc lie inS; their convex hull is centrally symmetric and has volume>=d^-d volS. Each halfspace throughc therefore removes at least alpha_d=1/[2^(d+1)*d!*d^d] of volK. After O_R(log(B/r0)) cuts, retaining the fixed ball would be impossible. Thus a good query occurs after poly_R(L+B) stages. All combinatorial vertex/simplex enumerations are polynomial for FIXEDd, with computable R-dependent exponents.

The arithmetic is also paid: round oracle normals to one fixed dyadic grid and rescale to integer normals of bit lengthQ=poly_R(L+B). Keep all offsets over a common denominator. Vertices are d-by-d rational solves; a new centroid/cut multiplies that denominator only by(d+1) and at most(d+1) determinants of these fixed-size integer-normal matrices. Its bit length increases O_R(Q) per stage, not exponentially by naive nested denominator
